annotations.note: Cooper's authorial introduction (heading literally 'Introduction'), explaining the Indian-name confusion (Mahicanni/Mohicans/Mohegans), the Lenni-Lenape vs Mengwe tribal map, and the coined 'Horican' for Lake George. TYPE JUDGMENT: heading says 'Introduction' so typed introduction, though Cooper himself calls it 'this preface' in its closing paragraph — soft preface/introduction boundary. This single block also serves the spec's 'notice on Indian names' function (no separate notice exists). Currently UNTYPED by the detector (no introduction element emitted).

annotations.count_cue: Exactly one verse/quotation epigraph opens every chapter — 33 chapters, 33 epigraphs (line-anchored /^Chapter (\d+)\n\n/ yields 33 heads numbered 1–33, and the first paragraph after each opens with a quote or ellipsis in all 33 cases, verified programmatically). 31 carry an em-dash attribution ('— Shakespeare', '— Bryant', '— Gray', '— Childe Harold', '— Pope's Iliad', '— Halleck', etc.); the 2 exceptions (Ch5 'Merchant of Venice', Ch7 'Gray') name the source directly after the closing quote with no em-dash — both are still genuine epigraphs. Sources span Shakespeare (Midsummer Night's Dream, Merchant of Venice, Othello, Lear, Henry V/VI, Julius Caesar, Twelfth Night, Much Ado), Pope's Iliad, Gray, Burns, Bryant, Byron (Childe Harold), Scott (Lady of the Lake), Parnell, Halleck. PRIMARY masked apparatus — the epigraph type is otherwise UNEXEMPLIFIED in the gold set; this work is the canonical exemplar.

annotations.note: PRIMARY structure for this contract. The detector emits no epigraph elements (by_type has none) and finds only 26 chapters, so the entire 33-instance epigraph layer is undetected/unmasked — it leaks into the running chapter body. Analogous to the chapter_heading apparatus in the scripture gold sets (idx100/idx101): a per-chapter masked masthead the detector folds into body text.

annotations.note: Cooper's collected explanatory notes under the heading 'Reference Notes' — 26 numbered notes (1–26, line-anchored /^\d+ / resolves 26× in this trailing block) on Indian dialects, Washington at the Monongahela, Narragansett pacers, scalping tuft, the long rifle, Glenn's Falls, Tamenund/Tammany, William Penn, etc. Keyed to inline superscript markers in the body (e.g. 'Horican.'1, 'tuft'4, 'yellow'5, 'river'7). Collected at the END of the work, so endnotes (not per-page footnotes). Currently UNTYPED/swallowed into the trailing body — detector emits no endnotes element.
